newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Empire East denies talk of cash troubles.
newsitem.headline: Empire East denies talk of cash troubles.

text.p: Empire East Land Holdings Inc, the housing development subsidiary of Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc, denied on Wednesday that the company was facing financial difficulties.
"All these rumours concerning our cash position, all of these are not true. Our company is very strong," said Giovanni Ng, investor relations officer of Megaworld and Empire East.
Stock market traders said speculation that Empire East was reeling from cash problems sent its share prices falling in Wednesday's trade.
Empire East closed 1.20 peso lower, or 12.37 percent, at 8.50 pesos. It was the third most actively traded issue.
Empire East president Gerardo Garcia told Reuters that he expected 33 percent growth in revenues and profits up to the year 2000.

"This year we hope to be able to realise almost two billion in profits... The annual demand for this medium-rise market is 100,000 to 150,000 units and we are not even satisfying it," said Garcia. Garcia said the company has one billion pesos of existing interest bearing loans against seven billion pesos worth of equity. None of the loans are due for payment, he said.
